new_jobs.title: Program Manager, GTM Systems
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic's GTM Systems team builds and operates the systems and processes behind the company's go-to-market motion — quoting, provisioning, customer success tooling, and the data infrastructure that ties them together. As a Program Manager on the team, you'll own cross-functional coordination across our concurrent systems initiatives: aligning stakeholders, running quarterly business reviews, and making sure every program stays tied to the business outcome it exists to drive.

You'll work across Sales, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and Business Technology leadership to keep multiple in-flight programs moving in lockstep — CPQ, deployment tracking, account data quality, and compliance-driven process change. You'll be the person in the room translating between technical implementation detail and executive priorities, and the person following up afterward to make sure alignment turns into action.

In a typical week, you'll prepare for and run quarterly business reviews, meet with operational leads and stakeholders across the GTM organization, and pull together the documentation that keeps initiatives aligned. Throughout, you'll dig into the "why" behind each program — not just tracking status, but making sure the team can always articulate the business outcome a program is meant to drive and how it's being measured.

Key Responsibilities

Own cross-functional coordination across concurrent GTM systems programs, including CPQ, deployment tracking, account data quality, and compliance-driven process change
Prepare and run quarterly business reviews for GTM systems initiatives, and drive the decisions and follow-ups that come out of them
Partner with operational leads and stakeholders across Sales, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and Business Technology to keep programs aligned and moving
Translate between technical implementation detail and executive priorities in both directions, so engineers understand the business context and leadership understands the trade-offs
Define and track the business outcome each program exists to drive, along with how it's measured, and hold programs to it
Aggregate and maintain the documentation, plans, and status views that keep cross-functional initiatives coherent
Surface risks, dependencies, and competing priorities early, and drive them to resolution without direct authority over the teams involved

Minimum Qualifications

Hands-on experience with GTM processes at a software or technology company — lead-to-cash, quote-to-cash, renewal and expansion motions, or customer health
Working understanding of how systems such as Salesforce, CPQ platforms, or customer success tools support those processes
A track record of owning cross-functional alignment with senior stakeholders — running recurring business reviews, facilitating rooms with competing priorities, and driving decisions without direct authority
Strong program management fundamentals: planning, tracking, dependency and risk management
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to move between technical detail and executive summary depending on the audience
Work effectively in fast-moving environments with high ambiguity, including where process doesn't exist yet
Excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with lead and campaign automation, CPQ implementations, or customer success and health-scoring programs (Gainsight or equivalent) at a software company
Experience operating in a compliance-sensitive environment, such as SOX or IPO readiness
Experience partnering closely with engineering or business technology teams on systems implementations, not only with business stakeholders
Familiarity with the data models behind GTM systems, and comfort using data to diagnose whether a program is working
Experience at a company that scaled significantly during your tenure

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$235,000—$300,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage:
Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

new_jobs.title: Office of Community Health Workers Tribal & Northern Coordinator (DOH/PHD/PCHB #55583)
new_jobs.description:
Salary

$27.37 - $41.06 Hourly

$56,931 - $85,396 Annually

This position is a Pay Band C7

Posting Details

THIS POSTING WILL BE USED FOR ONGOING RECRUITMENT AND MAY CLOSE AT ANY TIME. APPLICANT LISTS MAY BE SCREENED MORE THAN ONCE.

It is mission critical to the Governor's Priorities to reduce health disparities and improve health outcomes by providing access to care and services in support of health equity for New Mexicans.

The Office of Community Health Workers (OCHW) within the New Mexico Department of Health (NMDOH) exists to support the Community Health Workers/Representatives (CHW/R) profession and workforce development by leading strategic partnerships and capacity-building initiatives with organizations employing, training, and mentoring or advocating for Community Health Workers (CHWs) statewide.

Why does the job exist?

The position exists through annual legislative appropriations to meet the state mandated statutes: Senate Bill (SB) 58 enacting the Community Health Workers (CHW) Act and NMSA 1978 State-Tribal Collaboration Act.

The Office of Community Health Workers seeks to become a statewide convener for and is charged with workforce development through integration of Community Health Workers/Representatives into New Mexico's health and social service care teams and networks. This charge is key in providing a competent workforce by developing strategic partnerships across New Mexico with organizations employing, training, mentoring, and advocating for Community Health Workers/Representatives to support sustainability and workforce development initiatives for indigenous, rural and underserved, and northern communities within New Mexico.

This position will coordinate, direct, and deliver training, community outreach, and networking opportunities; develop social service and health care networks to support state health equity initiatives; and technical assistance to support state Community Health Worker/Representatives re/certification to individuals, communities, and organizations/providers in northern New Mexico and indigenous communities statewide.

How does it get done?

Key Position Responsibilities:

Responsible for coordinating, facilitating, and marketing Community Health Worker (CHW) state certification in the Northern and tribal communities of New Mexico.
Responsible for supporting CHW workforce recruitment efforts and activities during community events and/or via community requests in the Northern and tribal communities of New Mexico.
Responsible for identifying, coordinating, facilitating, and delivering content specific trainings for Community Health Workers/Representatives (CHW/Rs) monthly and/or conducting ad hoc presentations on various community issues and public health topics and trends in the Northern and tribal communities of New Mexico.
Responsible for developing and strengthening new and current social service and health care networks for tribal Community Health Representatives (CHR) and non-tribal Community Health Workers (CHWs), including CHW organizations/providers within northern New Mexico, rural and underserved, and indigenous communities statewide, including bordering states, cities, and towns.
Responsible for engaging, developing, and fostering collaborative working relationships and networks with northern and statewide Tribal Leadership and communities to align efforts that address social determinants of health, assist in resource allocation to improve health outcomes, and develop technical assistance supports for indigenous and northern communities, including bordering states.
Responsible for development of workplans for state certification and recruitment activities; professional development and training, community outreach and networking, and technical assistance supports for indigenous communities and non-Tribal organizations/providers in the Northern and tribal communities of New Mexico.
Responsible for planning and implementation of the statewide Office of Community Health Workers strategic plan components: regulations and workforce development, health and social care integration, organizational data systems and CHW/R engagement, and workforce sustainability; including data collection and reporting plans of indigenous, rural and underserved, and northern New Mexico communities.

Who are the customers?

Individuals and statewide, rural, frontier, and indigenous communities and regions, Community Health Workers/Representatives, Community Health Workers Affiliate organizations/providers, Federally Qualified Health Centers, Indian Health Service Units, Hospitals/Clinics, Public Health Offices, Community Based Organizations, Public School Systems, Higher Learning Institutions, Managed Care Organizations, and other health care and social service providers and networks.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate for the CHW Tribal and Northern Coordinator requires a unique blend of cultural humility, structural knowledge, and operational expertise. First and foremost a current New Mexico Certified Community Health Worker Certificate in good standing is necessary to be considered for this position.

Northern New Mexico presents a distinct landscape: a blend of historic Hispano communities alongside 19 Pueblo nations, the Jicarilla Apache Nation, and parts of the Navajo Nation. CHWs and CHRs serve as the primary bridge between these underserved areas and complex healthcare systems. The CHW-TNC will provide the training and technical assistance for them to be successful.

The ideal candidate will possess the following key characteristics:

Deep Literacy in Tribal Sovereignty and Community Health Representative(CHR) Frameworks

While CHWs and CHRs do similar frontline public health work, they operate under entirely different administrative umbrellas. The ideal CHW-TNC must understand these nuances.

Over 95% of CHR programs are directly operated by Tribes under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act. The CHW-TNC will respect tribal sovereignty and understand how the Indian Health Service (IHS) funds and guides these programs. They will know how to navigate tribal leadership hierarchies, respect traditional healing practices, and be adept at adapting health education materials so they are culturally appropriate for indigenous communities.

Expertise in New Mexico's Medicaid and Certification Ecosystem

The financial and regulatory landscape for New Mexico health workers has shifted significantly to allow greater autonomy. The ideal candidate has a firm grasp on Medicaid Reimbursement Pathways. They will be capable of training clinics and tribal health programs on how to utilize New Mexico¿s Medicaid standing orders. This includes navigating billing procedures so CHWs and CHRs can successfully bill for services like system navigation, health promotion, and clinical support without needing a direct clinician order for every visit.

Knowledgeable in State Certification Standards

The CHW-TNC will be well-versed in the New Mexico Department of Health Office of Community Health Workers (OCHW) certification process. They will be equipped to help workers accumulate the required Core Competencies and Continuing Education Units (CEUs) for state certification and recertification. When required, they will coordinate with the OCHW Training/Certification Team to provide technical assistance.

Competent in Rural, "Frontier" Delivery Models

Northern New Mexico is topographically diverse and highly rural. At times, traditional training and communication methods frequently fail due to limited broadband or long travel distances. The ideal provider should be adaptable for these situations. Mastery in deploying a "Customer Centered Use of Technology" will be expected. The CHW-TNC must be proficient in delivering both asynchronous (self-paced) online training and virtual communities of practice (similar to the Project ECHO model), while balancing these with vital, trust-building in-person site visits. This position will require frequent travel in-state.

Hold a Lived Understanding of Geographic Barriers

The CHW-TNC will understand the reality of frontier healthcare¿where a CHW/CHR¿s daily duties might range from vital-signs monitoring and health literacy coaching to chopping firewood, cleaning for an elder, or navigating unpaved roads during heavy winter mud.

Establish and Nurture Strong Local Academic and Non-Profit Partnerships

The ideal candidate should have experience establishing relationships with regional academic institutions anchored in CHW training, Community Health Worker advocacy groups and local non-profits and healthcare providers.

Capable of Appropriate Linguistic Integration

The ideal candidate will be bilingual in English and Spanish to effectively support Spanish-speaking community health networks and Community Health Workers. They must demonstrate a deep commitment to integrating indigenous language translators and protocols when working inside tribal entities.

Minimum Qualification

Associate degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Statistics, Finance, or a related field and two (2) years of experience with a public assistance program, medical, healthcare, educational, or state facility working with policies and procedures, conducting analysis/research, providing or requesting information from the general public, working with communities, working on health or social service related matters, social work/case management, behavioral health, and/or health care. Any combination of education from an accredited college or university in a related field and/or direct experience in this occupation totaling four (4) years may substitute for the required education and experience.

Employment Requirements

Must possess and maintain a valid Driver's License.

Must possess and maintain a current Defensive Driving Course Certification from the State of New Mexico or must pass and receive Defensive Driving Course Certification as a condition of continued employment.

Working Conditions

The working conditions for this position require splitting your time between an urban administrative office and hands-on, field-based community engagements across the state.

When you aren't on the road, your work is anchored at the New Mexico Department of Health (NMDOH) complex off San Mateo and Montgomery in Albuquerque. This is a professional state agency environment housing multiple core bureaus, including the Public Health Division's Population and Community Health teams. You will be operating in a standard office/cubicle setting handling data entry, compiling technical assistance modules, participating in regional state team meetings, and coordinating with state Medicaid and certification specialists. The office portion of the job is structured but fast-moving, requiring high digital proficiency to manage correspondence, track data for tribal and rural clinics, and host virtual training sessions or webinars,

The true heart of this role takes place outside the office. Frequent in-state travel in New Mexico means traversing vast, topographically diverse, and geographically isolated terrains to visit rural clinics, chapter houses, and Pueblo health community spaces. Expect significant highway and rural driving time. Travel to Northern New Mexico or tribal nations can easily involve multi-hour trips one-way, sometimes navigating unpaved roads, mountain passes, or unpredictable seasonal weather (monsoons in summer, snow/mud in winter). Once you arrive at a site, the environment shifts immediately from formal state administration to community-centric public health. You might be conducting an upskilling workshop in a community center, doing a walk-through with a CHR manager at a tribal clinic, or gathering feedback in a rural community room.

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking a Program Coordinator
to provide administrative and programmatic support to Suicide CPR Initiative program under the direction of a supervisor. Completes more routine tasks independently and relies on guidance from higher Program Manager (PM) levels for more complex tasks. This position is located in Bethesda, MD.

This position will be in support of the Suicide CPR Initiative program led by Dr. Marjan Holloway, a clinical psychologist and intervention scientist whose research focuses on developing and empirically evaluating innovative interventions to reduce suicide risk. The Initiative is uniquely positioned to address the critical issue of military suicide through its longstanding affiliation with the Uniformed Services University Health Sciences (USUHS), as well as its strong partnerships with the Department of Defense, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and national and international collaborators.

The Program Coordinator Will Support The Suicide Care, Prevention, And Research (SCPR) Initiative In The Medical And Clinical Psychology (MPS) Department Within The Uniformed Services University (USUHS) In Bethesda, Maryland. This Position Is Located At The Suicide CPR Initiative Office In Bethesda, Maryland (HJF Headquarters Building) And The Incumbent Will Be Expected To Work On-site 4 Days Per Week. The Mission Of The Suicide CPR Initiative Is Threefold

CARE: Develop and evaluate evidence-based interventions to reduce suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
PREVENTION: Save lives through education, intervention, scientific research, and advocacy.
RESEARCH: Advance the science and practice of suicide prevention and intervention to improve outcomes for service members, veterans, and other at-risk populations.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. The Program Coordinator assists with recruitment, BTC meetings seminar series and events, leadership calendars, equipment purchases, recruitment and travel arrangements.

Job Responsibilities

Provide dedicated administrative support to BTC, reporting to the BTC Scientific Director and supporting BTC leadership and programs. Interface between and support BTC clinical and research operations, including serving as the key liaison between research coordinators and clinical staff to ensure seamless care coordination for patients participating in research protocols. Additional duties include organizing inpatient clinical call schedules for faculty; organizing, facilitating, and documenting the weekly BTC multidisciplinary tumor board meeting; and developing and implementing BTC policies and procedures to address specific operational problems and improve patient care delivery.
Manage BTC core facilities and equipment, including coordinating with vendors for installation, maintenance, and repairs; overseeing equipment calendars; ordering and tracking supplies; managing service contracts; and handling billing for both BTC and external users.

Posted Job Title

Job Profile Title

Data Analyst C

Job Description Summary

Reporting to the Director of Public Health, the Data Analyst supports Public Health and Wellbeing’s mission of creating a community of care and the Wellness at Penn vision of integrating the science, theory, and practice of Wellness.

The Data Analyst fulfills this role by providing the Public Health and Wellbeing team with thoughtful assessment of undergraduate, graduate, and professional student data and clear and effective report writing to help tell the Wellness at Penn story. The Data Analyst manages multiple data systems and oversees survey administration as well as semester and annual population level data reviews that help tell the story of Wellness.

This position is responsible for gathering, analyzing, and communicating data that will provide Wellness at Penn with a data-driven, evidence-based approach to infusing wellness across its nine domains (Physical, emotional, social, spiritual, intellectual, occupation, environmental, creativity, and financial wellness) through inclusive, innovative, and impactful initiatives. The functions of this position include analyzing data to inform disease prevention efforts, identify patterns to help develop interventions, support evaluation of ongoing health and wellness programs, support a centralized method for evaluating, reporting, and managing transactions for student immunization and insurance requirements, and developing consistent processes and workflows in a new and evolving organization. This position will also collaborate closely with University data system operators including but not limited to Institutional Research and Advancement, Student Registration and Financial Services, and Data Warehouse, and Penn Medicine.

The Data Analyst will embrace our core values of compassion, accessibility, respect, and empowerment (CARE) throughout their work.

Job Description

Job Responsibilities

The Data Analyst Will

Oversee the analysis and reporting of population-level metrics on a monthly, semester and annual basis
Build, run, and perform routine analysis of data reports for population-level metrics using multiple data systems including electronic health record systems and national and university-based surveys
Assist public health surveillance reports monthly, semesterly, and annually
Support queries and workflows to manage and report student immunization and insurance requirements and transactions
Assist in evaluation frameworks and data analysis for health education programs and interventions
Evaluate and report on population level data acquired through Wellness at Penn services, including but not limited to:
Patient Satisfaction Surveys
National organization surveys and population level health assessments
General utilization of services
Create analysis plans and develop reports to present findings that inform University and Wellness colleagues on the health and wellness of Penn students
Develop innovative approaches for data sharing and visualization based on various audiences within the Penn community
Actively participate in relevant professional organizations
Other duties and responsibilities as assigned

Qualifications

Bachelor's and 2 to 3 years of experience or equivalent combination of education and experience is required; Master’s degree in public health or related field preferred.
Demonstrated organizational skills and ability to work on a team; excellent written communications skills.
Demonstrated ability to work across multiple data systems and to communicate effectively with diverse audiences, including students, faculty members, staff, and university administrators.
Experience with statistical analysis software (ex. SAS, SPSS, etc.) and electronic health record systems preferred.

new_jobs.title: Research Assistant
new_jobs.description:
Join Cleveland Clinic’s Main Campus where research and surgery are advanced, technology is leading-edge, patient care is world class and caregivers are family. Here, you will work alongside a passionate and dedicated team, receive endless support and appreciation, and build a rewarding career with one of the most respected healthcare organizations in the world.

Innovative and groundbreaking discoveries happen every day at Cleveland Clinic. Each member of our team contributes to our mission of caring for life, researching health and educating those who serve. As a Research Assistant, you will help facilitate this vision by assisting with the implementation and conduct of human subject research projects.

A caregiver in this position works days from 7:00 a.m. -- 7:30 p.m.,
25–35 hours per week.

A caregiver who excels in this role will:

Assist research team with research study related tasks.
Assist with completion of protocol related activities.
Obtain and maintain clinical competencies such as phlebotomy, vital signs, ECG, POC testing and other testing as required.
Assist with the development and coordination of the research subject schedule in compliance with the research protocol.
Assist with the collection, recording and maintenance of research study records.
Demonstrate comprehension of assigned research protocols.
Develop and maintain knowledge of research protocols to coordinate the comprehensive and compliant execution of assigned protocols.
May assist in the development and maintenance of research tools, such as spreadsheets, questionnaires and/or brochures.
Maintain study personnel certification records (License, CV, CITI).
Establish and maintain filing systems.
Order and stock supplies.
Maintain professional relationships, including frequent and open effective communication with internal and external customers.
Perform other duties as assigned.

High School Diploma/GED
Demonstrated proficiency with a variety of computer-based skills, including Word processing, spreadsheets, and database and presentation software
Understand basic concept of study design
Strong organizational, communication and interpersonal skills

One year of experience in a healthcare setting OR Bachelor’s Degree
Knowledge of medical terminology

UPMC is hiring a Casual Research Assistant to support our team at the Magee Womens Research Institute (MWRI) team at Magee Womens Hospital! This position will be scheduled to work Monday, Tuesdays, and Thursdays from 7:00am to 2:00pm with some flexibility. No evenings, weekends, or holidays required. We are looking for someone who is hard working, punctual, dependable, interacts well with patients and staff, and pays good attention to detail.

Responsibilities:

Organize references and materials for research projects and content areas.
Maintain professionalism in all interactions with stakeholders and internal staff.
Conduct literature searches.
Provide support for grant proposal and manuscript development and submission.
Participate in meetings, trainings and seminars, both internally and externally.
Perform data collection and entry.
Assist in data management.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in a related field, or current enrollment, with some experience in research environment.

Experience in the area of public health, psychology, applied research or behavioral health is preferred. Strong written and verbal skills. Detail oriented. Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Access and the ability to learn various software packages as needed.
